cases.patientSummary: Male, 39, Ahmedabad — 10 months of fatigue, progressive splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia
cases.caseText:
Patient: Male, 39 years old, Ahmedabad, Gujarat
Family: Parents are first cousins (consanguineous marriage)

Presenting complaints (10 months):
- Progressively worsening fatigue and weakness
- Dragging sensation and visible fullness in the left upper abdomen
- Frequent bruising; 2 episodes of spontaneous nosebleed
- No fever, no lymphadenopathy

Findings:
- Massive splenomegaly (spleen palpable 12 cm below costal margin)
- Hepatomegaly (liver 4 cm below costal margin)
- CBC: Hb 8.2, Platelet 54,000, WBC 3.1
- LFTs mildly elevated (AST 52, ALT 61)
- Bone pain reported in bilateral femurs

Previous diagnoses (all incorrect): Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, chronic malarial splenomegaly

cases.patientSubmittedText:
Age: 28
Sex: Male
State: Maharashtra
Symptom onset: 2015-03-28
Family history: My maternal uncle (mama) died at 42 of kidney failure — doctors said "unknown cause." My mother has occasional pain in her     
  ▎ hands but much milder than mine. My grandmother (nani) on my mother's side had heart problems.
Symptoms (in patient's own words):
  ▎ For the last 6 years (started around age 22), I get these episodes of intense burning pain in my hands and feet — like fire,   
  ▎ like hot needles. It comes and goes, often triggered by exercise, fever, or hot weather. Most doctors have told me it's 
  ▎ anxiety. I've taken painkillers, ayurvedic treatments, physiotherapy. Nothing changes the pattern.                             
  ▎                                                                                                                                
  ▎ I sweat very little — even when everyone around me is sweating from the Mumbai heat, I just feel hot but my body doesn't sweat.
  ▎  My mother always said I was "just dry-skinned" since I was a teenager.                                                        
  ▎                                                                  
  ▎ I have small dark red spots on my lower back and around my belly button — like tiny dots, flat, not raised. A skin doctor said 
  ▎ they were "just freckles." They've been increasing slowly. Some sit just below the swimsuit line.
  ▎                                                                                                                                
  ▎ In the last year I'm tired faster, my heart sometimes races for no reason, and my urine occasionally looks foamy. A GP said my 
  ▎ creatinine was "borderline high" and told me to drink more water.

cases.caseText:
--- Patient's own description ---
Age: 28
Sex: Male
State: Maharashtra
Symptom onset: 2015-03-28
Family history: My maternal uncle (mama) died at 42 of kidney failure — doctors said "unknown cause." My mother has occasional pain in her     
  ▎ hands but much milder than mine. My grandmother (nani) on my mother's side had heart problems.
Symptoms (in patient's own words):
  ▎ For the last 6 years (started around age 22), I get these episodes of intense burning pain in my hands and feet — like fire,   
  ▎ like hot needles. It comes and goes, often triggered by exercise, fever, or hot weather. Most doctors have told me it's 
  ▎ anxiety. I've taken painkillers, ayurvedic treatments, physiotherapy. Nothing changes the pattern.                             
  ▎                                                                                                                                
  ▎ I sweat very little — even when everyone around me is sweating from the Mumbai heat, I just feel hot but my body doesn't sweat.
  ▎  My mother always said I was "just dry-skinned" since I was a teenager.                                                        
  ▎                                                                  
  ▎ I have small dark red spots on my lower back and around my belly button — like tiny dots, flat, not raised. A skin doctor said 
  ▎ they were "just freckles." They've been increasing slowly. Some sit just below the swimsuit line.
  ▎                                                                                                                                
  ▎ In the last year I'm tired faster, my heart sometimes races for no reason, and my urine occasionally looks foamy. A GP said my 
  ▎ creatinine was "borderline high" and told me to drink more water.

--- Doctor's clinical observations ---
 Examination (28M, Mumbai):                                                                                                     
  ▎ - Multiple punctate angiokeratomas on lower back, periumbilical, and "swimsuit" distribution — bilateral
  ▎ - Hypohidrosis confirmed on history; reduced palmar sweating on exam                                                           
  ▎ - Slit-lamp ophthalmology: bilateral corneal whorl-like opacities (cornea verticillata) noted
  ▎ - BP 142/90 (elevated); echo shows mild concentric LVH                                                                         
  ▎ - Urine: 2+ proteinuria; serum creatinine 1.4 mg/dL                                                                            
  ▎ - Neuro: distal small-fibre sensory loss to pinprick on hands/feet; otherwise normal                                           
  ▎ - Family pedigree: classic X-linked recessive pattern (maternal uncle ESRD, mild affected mother, maternal grandmother cardiac)

screener.screener_note: This 28-year-old male presents with a 6-year history of acral neuropathic pain, confirmed hypohidrosis, pathognomonic corneal verticillata on slit-lamp, punctate angiokeratomas in typical distribution, and progressive renal/cardiac involvement. The family pedigree (X-linked ESRD in maternal uncle, mild phenotype in heterozygous mother) and the multi-system constellation are diagnostic red flags for Fabry disease (α-galactosidase A deficiency). Proceed immediately to plasma/leucocyte α-galactosidase A activity and GLA gene sequencing. This is a rare disease that explains the complete picture and carries treatment implications (enzyme replacement therapy, chaperone therapy).
common_conditions_considered: Anxiety disorder (initially diagnosed by multiple doctors)
Chronic kidney disease of unknown etiology

unified_differential.disease_name: Fabry Disease (Anderson-Fabry Disease, α-galactosidase A deficiency)
supporting_features: Pathognomonic triad: thermosensitive acroparesthesia (burning pain in hands/feet triggered by exercise, fever, heat) + angiokeratoma corporis diffusum in classic swimsuit/periumbilical/lower-back distribution + palmoplantar hypohidrosis since adolescence
Cornea verticillata on slit-lamp — near-pathognomonic in an unmedicated young male (amiodarone/chloroquine excluded); seen in >90% of classic hemizygous males
Distal small-fibre sensory neuropathy on examination — Gb3 accumulation in dorsal root ganglia (Aδ and C fibres)
Early Fabry nephropathy: moderate proteinuria (2+), borderline creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, hypertension — Gb3 in podocytes/tubular cells
Concentric LVH on echocardiography with episodic tachycardia — early Fabry cardiomyopathy in 3rd-4th decade
Textbook X-linked recessive pedigree: maternal uncle ESRD at 42 (hemizygous), mother with mild hand pain (obligate carrier), maternal grandmother with cardiac disease
Multi-system involvement (neuro + derm + renal + cardiac) explained by a single locus (GLA)
Classic 6-year diagnostic delay misattributed to anxiety — matches global Fabry diagnostic odyssey pattern
Age 28 male at canonical inflection point in untreated classic Fabry natural history
non_matching_features: No GI symptoms (diarrhoea, post-prandial pain) — present in ~50% of classic Fabry; absence does not argue against diagnosis
No stroke/TIA yet — expected later in natural history
Enzyme activity, lyso-Gb3 and GLA genotype not yet confirmed — diagnosis is clinical at this stage

confirmatory_tests.test: Urine sediment for mulberry cells (Maltese cross inclusions on polarised/phase-contrast microscopy)
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Highly specific supportive finding for Fabry nephropathy. Cheap, fast adjunct.

confirmatory_tests.test: Leukocyte or dried-blood-spot α-galactosidase A (α-Gal A) enzyme activity assay
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: DEFINITIVE in hemizygous males: <1% activity confirms classic Fabry; 1–10% suggests late-onset variant. Result in 5–10 days. NOT reliable in carrier females.
Highly sensitive biomarker; elevated in virtually all classic Fabry males (often >10 nmol/L vs normal <2). Tracks treatment response. Preferred when enzyme is borderline.

confirmatory_tests.test: GLA gene full sequencing + del/dup analysis
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Confirms causative variant; required for cascade screening of mother/female relatives, migalastat amenability assessment, and ERT documentation.

confirmatory_tests.test: MRI brain with FLAIR (white matter and pulvinar sign screening)
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Detects silent cerebrovascular disease and pulvinar T1 hyperintensity (Fabry feature). Baseline before ERT.

confirmatory_tests.test: Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Inferolateral LGE pattern is characteristic of Fabry cardiomyopathy and distinguishes it from hypertensive/sarcomeric HCM. Essential baseline before ERT.

confirmatory_tests.test: Skin biopsy with EM (zebra bodies) — only if enzyme/genetics equivocal
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Lamellar Gb3 inclusions in vascular endothelium. Not needed if enzyme + genetics confirmatory.

confirmatory_tests.test: Kidney biopsy with EM — only if needed to stage nephropathy
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Pathognomonic zebra bodies in podocytes. Defer until after enzyme/genetic confirmation.

confirmatory_tests.test: GLA cascade testing in mother and maternal relatives
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Mother is obligate carrier; enzyme is unreliable in females so sequencing is required. Maternal uncle's children urgently need screening.

supporting_features: Episodic burning pain in hands and feet triggered by heat and exercise — superficial overlap with Fabry acroparesthesia
Small-fibre neuropathy phenotype (Nav1.7 expressed in DRG)
Maternal hand pain could theoretically represent mild AD expression
non_matching_features: Autosomal dominant SCN9A inheritance is incompatible with the X-linked pedigree (maternal uncle ESRD, carrier mother)
Erythromelalgia produces visible erythema/warmth during attacks — not described here
No angiokeratomas, no cornea verticillata, no nephropathy, no LVH — none explained by SCN9A
Hypohidrosis is not a feature; if anything, hyperhidrosis is more typical
Accounts for 1 of 11 HPO terms; Fabry accounts for all 11

confirmatory_tests.test: SCN9A gene sequencing — only if Fabry conclusively excluded
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Low yield in this case; reserved as diagnostic exercise if α-Gal A and GLA sequencing return negative.

unified_differential.disease_name: Kanzaki Disease (α-N-Acetylgalactosaminidase deficiency / Schindler Type II)
supporting_features: Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum mirroring Fabry distribution
Adult-onset lysosomal storage disorder with peripheral neuropathy
Distal sensory impairment can be reported
non_matching_features: Autosomal recessive (NAGA) — incompatible with X-linked pedigree
No cornea verticillata, no significant renal/cardiac storage at this severity
Extremely rare (<30 reported cases worldwide); mild cognitive impairment usually expected

confirmatory_tests.test: Leukocyte NAGA enzyme activity — only if α-Gal A activity is normal
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Second-line exclusionary test; biallelic NAGA mutations on sequencing required for confirmation.

supporting_features: Can produce angiokeratomas in a distribution similar to Fabry disease
non_matching_features: Autosomal recessive (FUCA1) — incompatible with X-linked pedigree
Causes progressive intellectual disability, coarse facies, dysostosis multiplex — none present
No cornea verticillata, no acroparesthesia, no significant nephropathy
Included only as an angiokeratoma mimic; clinically excluded

confirmatory_tests.test: Plasma α-L-fucosidase enzyme activity — only if Fabry excluded
confirmatory_tests.yield_level: Not indicated in this case; included for differential completeness.

recommended_tests.name: Urine sediment for mulberry cells (phase-contrast/polarised microscopy)
recommended_tests.rationale: Cheapest possible Fabry-specific finding. Lipid-laden tubular epithelial cells with Maltese-cross birefringence are highly specific for Fabry nephropathy and can be done at any laboratory with phase-contrast microscopy today.

recommended_tests.name: Leukocyte or dried-blood-spot α-galactosidase A (α-Gal A) enzyme activity assay
recommended_tests.rationale: Single most decisive test for this hemizygous male. <1% activity = classic Fabry; result in 5–10 days. Order TODAY — do not wait for genetics. Available via DBS shipped to NIRMAN Mumbai, Medgenome, AIIMS Metabolic Lab, or Manipal.

recommended_tests.name: Plasma lyso-Gb3 (globotriaosylsphingosine) by LC-MS/MS
recommended_tests.rationale: Highly sensitive Fabry biomarker (often >10 nmol/L in classic males vs normal <2). Confirms enzyme result, baselines disease activity, and tracks ERT response. Useful in carrier females where enzyme is unreliable.

recommended_tests.name: MRI brain with FLAIR sequences
recommended_tests.rationale: Baseline screen for silent white-matter disease and pulvinar sign. Required before ERT initiation; cerebrovascular events are a major Fabry morbidity.

recommended_tests.name: GLA gene full sequencing + deletion/duplication analysis
recommended_tests.rationale: Required for: (1) precise mutation identification, (2) migalastat amenability assessment, (3) cascade testing of mother and maternal relatives (enzyme unreliable in females), (4) ERT/named-patient programme documentation.

recommended_tests.name: Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement
recommended_tests.rationale: Inferolateral LGE differentiates Fabry cardiomyopathy from hypertensive/sarcomeric HCM. Essential baseline before ERT and for cardiac risk stratification (sudden death from arrhythmia).

recommended_tests.name: GLA cascade screening in mother and maternal lineage
recommended_tests.rationale: Mother is an obligate carrier; maternal uncle's children are at 50% risk. Genetic counselling for the entire maternal lineage is essential. Sequencing required (enzyme unreliable in females).

recommended_tests.name: Skin or kidney biopsy with electron microscopy
recommended_tests.rationale: Reserved for cases where enzyme/genetics are equivocal, or where renal staging is needed to escalate ERT urgency. Demonstrates pathognomonic zebra bodies.

aiResult.specialist_type_recommended: Adult Metabolic Geneticist (Lysosomal Storage Disorder specialist) with multidisciplinary co-management by Nephrology and Cardiology; Clinical Geneticist for cascade family screening and counselling
referral_centers: AIIMS New Delhi — Department of Medical Genetics and Metabolic Disease Clinic (α-Gal A enzyme assay and GLA sequencing in-house; ERT-experienced)
CMC Vellore — Clinical Genetics Unit and Department of Nephrology (Fabry ERT programme experience and multidisciplinary monitoring)
Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Mumbai — Adult Metabolic Disease and Fabry ERT centre (closest to patient's geography)
KEM Hospital Mumbai — Clinical Genetics and Nephrology (local Mumbai access for biopsy and follow-up)
CDFD Hyderabad / Medgenome Bangalore — Molecular GLA sequencing and lyso-Gb3 reference testing (DBS samples can be shipped from Mumbai)
aiResult.case_conference_narrative: This 28-year-old man from Mumbai has a 6-year history of burning pain in his hands and feet triggered by heat and exercise, with reduced sweating, 'freckle-like' angiokeratomas across his swimsuit area, whorl-like opacities on the cornea (cornea verticillata), and now early kidney damage (proteinuria, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL), high blood pressure, and thickening of the heart muscle — a constellation that Fabry disease (OMIM 301500, X-linked α-galactosidase A deficiency) explains completely and that no common disease explains. Both the Neurogenetic and Immunologic specialists independently assign 97% confidence, and the family pedigree (maternal uncle dead of kidney failure at 42, mother with mild hand pain, grandmother with heart disease) is a textbook X-linked Fabry pattern; the metabolic specialist report failed to return but does not change the picture, as two specialists already converge on the same diagnosis with no disagreement. Immediate next step today: send a dried-blood-spot α-galactosidase A enzyme activity assay (₹3,000–8,000, result in 5–10 days via NIRMAN Mumbai, Medgenome, or AIIMS) — in a hemizygous male, activity below 1% is essentially diagnostic and unlocks enzyme replacement therapy (agalsidase) or oral migalastat. While awaiting the result, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB for proteinuria, begin carbamazepine or gabapentin for the neuropathic pain (NSAIDs/opioids have failed because this is Gb3-mediated, not nociceptive), and arrange GLA sequencing for the patient and his mother. This is urgent: untreated, his maternal uncle's trajectory of end-stage renal disease at 42 is the natural history he is on, and ERT initiated now can slow renal and cardiac progression.

consultations.requestNote: Patient is 39, starting ERT. Any guidance on imiglucerase dosing and GBA sequencing for family planning?
consultations.specialistNotes:
Recommend starting imiglucerase at 60 U/kg IV every 2 weeks. GBA sequencing appropriate for family planning — recommend testing siblings and children of patient. Standard N370S and L444P panel first at CDFD Hyderabad.

Regarding the Neurogenetic agent's concern about NPC-C: the crumpled tissue-paper BM morphology and the dramatic response pattern here effectively rule it out clinically. I would not order filipin staining. The N370S variant is overwhelmingly the most common Gujarati GBA pathogenic variant.
